payload.rationale: Early September EIA data shows a sharp increase in retail gasoline prices, rising from $4.207 on August 31 to $4.455 on September 14, an increase of nearly 6%. September historically features a strong positive seasonal adjustment for gasoline, typically adding 2 to 2.5 percentage points to the non-seasonally adjusted change. With gasoline holding a 3.77% relative importance weight, a seasonally adjusted gasoline increase of 6% to 8% would alone contribute 0.2% to 0.3% to the headline CPI. Assuming core CPI continues to rise at its recent trend of 0.2% to 0.3%, the headline CPI is highly likely to print at 0.4% or higher, easily exceeding the 0.2% threshold (which requires a rounded 0.3% or higher). The primary risk is a sudden collapse in late-September energy prices or an anomalously weak core print, but the strong early-month energy data provides a substantial buffer.
limitations: Only early-to-mid September gasoline data is available; late-September prices are unknown.
EIA weekly prices are an approximation and do not perfectly map to the BLS CPI gasoline index.
Core CPI components (like shelter or used cars) could unexpectedly drag down the headline number.
